::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Which sans serif and monospace fonts suit Century Schoolbook?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/13598/which-sans-serif-and-monospace-fonts-suit-century-schoolbook), asked by [Andrey Vihrov](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3104/andrey-vihrov) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-16; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I find the [Century Schoolbook][q-1] family very legible for online documentation. However, I am unsure what [sans serif][q-2] (for typesetting, e.g., LaTeX package names) and [monospace][q-3] (for typesetting code) counterparts to choose for use with this typeface.
>
> Which fonts, in your opinion, could (and could not) be used with Century Schoolbook?
>
>   [q-1]: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_Type_Family#Century_Schoolbook
>   [q-2]: http://www.tug.dk/FontCatalogue/sansseriffonts.html
>   [q-3]: http://www.tug.dk/FontCatalogue/typewriterfonts.html
:::

Ironic that you find Century Schoolbook suitable for online documentation, as it was developed nearly 100 years ago for school textbooks!

While googling I found [esperfonto](http://www.esperfonto.com/), which has a search box to help pair fonts.

They [suggest](http://www.esperfonto.com/search.html?typeface=&body=on&sans=on&workswith=Century+Schoolbook) Arial, Helvetica, or Frutiger Humanist 777 for sans fonts.  They don't suggest monospace pairs, though.

The Frutiger family is not free.  I tried Century Schoolbook, Helvetica, and Courier, and it seems to look pretty good.  

Here is a sample document (requires `xelatex`) to test your selections:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\title{Font Test}
\usepackage[english]{babel}
\usepackage{blindtext}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{Century Schoolbook}
\setsansfont{Helvetica}
\setmonofont{Courier}
\usepackage{sectsty}
\allsectionsfont{\sffamily}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

This article uses the \textsf{blindtext} package to typeset dummy text.  The preamble is:

\begin{verbatim}
\documentclass{article}
\title{Font Test}
\usepackage[english]{babel}
\usepackage{blindtext}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\setmainfont{Century Schoolbook}
\setsansfont{Arial}
\usepackage{sectsty}
\setmonofont{Courier}
\allsectionsfont{\sffamily}
\end{verbatim}
\blinddocument
\end{document}
```
